Done. Here's a summary of what happened:

## Rollback completed ✅

**Situation:** checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all production regions with an 18% error rate. Deployment history showed v2.3.0 was the most recent release healthy in production (v2.3.1-rc never went to production).

**Action taken:**
1. Rolled back to **v2.3.0**. The first attempt partially failed (orchestrator error) and only reached us-east, so I retried — the second attempt completed the rollout to us-west and eu-west.
2. **Verified recovery:** all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) are now on v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate dropped from 18% to 0.2%.

**Incident:** The incident creation call initially timed out, but verification via `list_incidents` confirmed it was actually created successfully (no duplicate retry needed):
- **INC-0001** (SEV2, open): "checkout-api v2.3.1 unhealthy in production — rolled back to v2.3.0", with full details of the failure, rollback steps, and the partial-failure/retry, plus a note that root cause of v2.3.1 needs investigation.

No change-manager approval was needed since v2.3.0 had previously been healthy in production.
